comparison: Both evaluate RNA sequencing results (C8, C40-C42). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED with appropriate methods and deposition. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging 'valuable dataset' but expressing concern about annotation methods being 'briefly described' and calling for 'further validation of predicted lncRNAs.'

Both assess differential expression analysis (C9, C10, C19, C20). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical methods. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging the analysis without methodological concerns as part of 'overall solid methodology.'

Both address WGCNA results and t-SNE model (C11, C12, C27). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED for module construction and clustering. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, explicitly stating the '60-gene t-SNE model successfully differentiated' groups 'with high specificity and sensitivity.'

OpenEval R9 evaluates t-SNE clustering (C12) as SUPPORTED. This overlaps with peer R3 which also addresses C12 and rates it SUPPORTED, recognizing the model's ability to distinguish groups as a study strength.

OpenEval evaluates CRC prediction ROC results (C35, C36) as SUPPORTED with validation in independent cohort. Peer R4 addresses broader classification claims (C13, C35-C39) and rates UNCERTAIN, noting validation cohort size 'is not enough' and requesting 'external validation' and analysis of only T1 patients.

OpenEval evaluates AA prediction (C37) as SUPPORTED, noting substantial improvement over current methods. Peer R4 includes C37 in broader UNCERTAIN evaluation, expressing concerns about validation cohort size and composition.

Both evaluate QDA classification performance (C13, C38, C39). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with high sensitivity important for screening. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about validation cohort size and requesting analysis using only T1 patients since 'only half were T1 stage.'

Both assess sEV characterization (C14-C17). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting proper MISEV2018 guidelines and multiple validation methods. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED without raising concerns, implicitly accepting as part of 'overall solid methodology.'

Both evaluate clustering and pathway enrichment (C18, C21). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate qualifications about imperfect separation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, treating findings as part of accepted analytical framework.

Both assess ssGSEA and microenvironmental analysis (C22-C26). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED though notes C26 is interpretive. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging contribution to understanding sEV-RNAs' role without methodological concerns.

Both evaluate miRNA clustering observation (C28). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as reasonable inference about coordinated regulation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting the multi-RNA type approach as part of comprehensive profiling.

Both assess module-trait correlations (C30-C34). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with RT-qPCR validation strengthening findings. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, not directly challenging correlations but requesting 'performance analysis across different demographic and tumor pathology factors' to validate clinical utility.

Both evaluate novelty claims (C44, C45). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting claims cannot be fully verified without exhaustive literature review. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging as 'proof-of-principle study' with 'valuable' dataset without challenging novelty.

Both assess study cohorts (C50-C53). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes small discovery cohort and control selection as potential limitations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising significant concerns that validation cohort is 'only half T1 patients' and size 'is not enough to obtain accurate evaluation.'

Both evaluate main conclusions (C68-C70). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by comprehensive data though notes C70 is speculative. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging study 'highlights potential' but emphasizing findings 'would benefit from further validation' in larger cohorts.
